com.minecolonies.coremod.info.com.coloni: Introduction

The Wall Tower is a guard post that stands in a wall: the walk runs through it at head height, so a rampart butted into either side carries straight on. Its men patrol the wall itself, turning at the next tower, and they see further than men on the ground.
Its level is how many guards it holds, Knights or Rangers in any mix; the Watchmen research adds more. Tower guards defend the town; the War Room's men are the ones who leave.
The Patrol

With Walk the wall on (in the settings) the tower lays a line of patrol points along the wall it stands on, eight blocks apart, and puts its guards on manual patrol. The line comes from the colony's own wall register, so a wall that grows is walked as it grows; a stretch of somebody else's wall - a style pack's - is counted but not walked.
Turn it off for a tower on a gate, or while the wall is still being built: then it is an ordinary guard tower with a good view.
The Wall

A wall is built out of the mod's own pieces - palisade, stone rampart, fortified rampart - or out of any style pack's walls. Every piece registers itself with the colony, so nobody has to stand near it to be counted.
Coverage is how much of the ring round the town has wall in it; strength is height by tier, per column. A closed two-high stone ring scores 69, the same ring five high 100. Walls are hard, not invincible: a wall you cannot lose is a wall nobody attacks.
Introduction

The War Room is where a colony decides its wars and hires the men who fight them. It hires Knights and Rangers the way the Barracks does - 2, 4, 6, 9 and 12 by level, in any mix - and one Explorer.
Tower guards defend; War Room guards leave. A colony that empties its towers to march is a colony a thief can walk into.
Its tabs: the war table, expeditions, the convoy and the walls. Everything on them is also a /war command.
The War Table

The table lists everything a warband could march on - colonies, kingdoms, the nearest raider camp and village - nearest first, with distance, direction, strength and standing.
March is lit only when the men could go; the small print says why not. The second button is whatever else there is to do with that neighbour: Peace, Accept, Withdraw, Ally or Convoy.
Above them: how many go, Recall, Ransom for the men held, Hire for sellswords. Below, the war log.
War

Standing falls only when somebody is caught at something; it never drifts. Low standing unlocks a declaration but never makes one: /war declare <colony> plunder, raze or conquer - the goal says what the victor may take.
The men walk the map like the Nether Worker. Where somebody is playing the town it is a real raid at its walls; where nobody is, strength against strength with luck. Marching costs two rations a man and wears both towns down; above 60 the men refuse to go.
Peace

Peace is a negotiation. One side offers terms - Peace on the table, or /war offer: a white peace, tribute (their gold), pay (yours) or their vassalage - and the other accepts or refuses within two days. Accepting moves the gold, sends every captive on both sides home and starts a truce.
Standing of 40 unlocks Ally. Allies cannot declare on each other and their convoys carry three times the goods. Breaking it drops the standing to nothing.
Convoys

A convoy carries what is on the convoy tab's manifest. Load the goods you want to send - a stack a press, up to the cap - and the couriers bring them from the warehouse to the War Room; or carry them there yourself.
Once they are in, Convoy beside a neighbour on the war table sends them with the escort you choose. Arriving, they go into the partner's warehouse and standing rises: twice a week per partner, never at war. A kingdom also forgives a reprisal it owed you.
Sellswords

Hire on the war table buys sellswords for gold out of the warehouse, up to two a level of the room. They wait three days at the War Room for the next warband and go with it, six strength a man; in a raid fought in the world they stand on the field beside the guards.
They are not citizens and cannot be held captive, and they take their share of the plunder: a stack for every two of them.
Expeditions

The Explorer goes out to look, not to fight. The Expeditions tab lists every kind of country within reach - forest, jungle, desert, mountains, ocean, the caves - with the biome found and how far. Pick a difficulty and an escort and press Go.
He brings home the land's goods and whatever the beasts there dropped. Harder means more of both and more danger; driven off, the men drop half of it and come home hurt. Everyone who went learns from it.
Walls

The walls tab shows every piece of wall the colony has ordered and what stands. Take a Wall Planner, mark two corners, and the Builder does the rest; the score is coverage and height by tier - palisade, stone, fortified. A Wall Tower's men walk the wall.
Research, in the Combat tree under A Standing Army: Drill for more soldiers, Find the Raiders for an alarm that sends every guard at a raid, Hue and Cry for posted guards, Watchmen and Masonry for the walls.
Depth

warLevel in the server config says how far a war may go. Skirmish: warbands and plunder, but no breaches, no captives, no sellswords; raze and conquer refused. Siege, the default: breaches, captives and ransom, sellswords. Conquest: also the goal conquer - a town overrun is the victor's vassal for seven days, pays two stacks of goods a day out of its warehouse, cannot march on its lord and is let go by /war release. Nobody's colony changes hands.
